ASNT Level III Exam Overview

The ASNT Level III certification requires passing two examinations — the Basic exam and the Method exam — for each method in which you certify.

ComponentDetails
Basic exam135 multiple-choice questions on materials science, NDE processes, and quality/certification standards (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189)
Method (Specific) examMethod-specific multiple-choice exam, typically 60–80 questions
FormatComputer-based testing at Prometric / Pearson VUE centers
Passing score70% for the Basic exam; 80% for the Method exam
Time limit4 hours (Basic); 2–3 hours (Method, varies by method)
Retake policy30-day wait between attempts; three attempts per 12-month period
Validity5-year certification cycle with renewal requirements

Important: the ASNT Level 3 Basic exam only needs to be passed once. You can then add additional methods by passing only the Method exam for each new method.

Method Exam Topic Areas

Ultrasonic Testing (UT): wave modes and propagation, acoustic impedance, Snell's law and mode conversion, near/far field and beam spread, attenuation, transducer types, straight- and angle-beam techniques, DAC/TCG and DGS, TOFD and phased array principles, calibration blocks (IIW, DSC, V1/V2), ASME Section V Article 4, and AWS D1.1 acceptance criteria.

Radiographic Testing (RT): X-ray and gamma sources (Ir-192, Co-60, Se-75), radiation physics, inverse square law and exposure calculations, half-value layers, film characteristics and processing, CR/DR, IQIs, geometric unsharpness, exposure techniques, interpretation, ALARA radiation safety, and ASME Section V Article 2.

Magnetic Particle Testing (MT): flux density and permeability, hysteresis, magnetization methods (yoke, prods, coil, central conductor), ampere-turn calculations, particle types, continuous vs residual method, demagnetization, system performance checks (Ketos ring, QQI, pie gauge), and ASME Section V Article 7.

Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT): penetrant types and removal methods A–D, sensitivity levels, capillary action, dwell and development times, developer types, UV-A and white-light requirements, TAM/PSM-5 performance checks, and ASME Section V Article 6.

Visual Testing (VT): vision and light measurement, direct and remote examination, weld gauges, discontinuity identification, minimum illumination (50 fc / 500 lux), Jaeger near-vision requirements, AWS D1.1 visual criteria, and ASME Section V Article 9.

Eddy Current Testing (ET): electromagnetic induction and skin depth, impedance plane analysis, frequency selection, lift-off and fill factor, probe types, ECA, tube inspection, conductivity sorting, and ASME Section V Article 8.

Key Standards to Study

Focus on ASME BPVC Section V (Articles 1, 2, 4–9, 23) plus the acceptance criteria in the referencing code (e.g., ASME Section VIII Div 1 UW-51/52 and Appendix 8); ASTM standards adopted into Section V (E94, E164, E165, E709, E1444, E1816, E2700); and AWS D1.1 Clause 6 with its UT acceptance tables, AWS B1.10, and AWS QC1. Know the differences between SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, and ISO 9712.

Study Strategy — 3 to 6 Months

PhaseDurationFocus
1. FoundationWeeks 1–4Materials science, metallurgy, NDE overview; ASNT Level III Study Guide: Basic
2. Standards deep diveWeeks 5–10Read applicable code sections cover to cover; summarise each Article
3. Method masteryWeeks 11–16Method-specific topics and calculations
4. Practice examsWeeks 17–20Timed practice; identify and restudy weak areas
5. Final reviewWeeks 21–24Formulas, code paragraphs, repeat practice exams

Common Failure Areas

Candidates most often lose points on calculations (near field, beam spread, geometric unsharpness, Snell's law), code interpretation (acceptance tables, shall/should/may), materials science (Fe-C phase diagram, heat treatment, hydrogen cracking, fatigue), and certification programs (SNT-TC-1A vs CP-189 vs ISO 9712).

Exam Day Tips

Bring photo ID, confirmation, and a non-programmable calculator — the exam is closed book. Arrive 30 minutes early. Budget roughly 1.8 minutes per Basic question and 2 minutes per Method question; flag hard questions and return later. Answer every question — there is no guessing penalty. Watch for "EXCEPT" wording, estimate calculation answers before solving, and check units.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is on the ASNT Level 3 Basic exam?

The Basic exam covers three areas: certification programs (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712 and written practices), general familiarity with all common NDT methods, and materials, fabrication, and product technology — metallurgy, welding processes, and discontinuity formation. It is 135 questions with a 4-hour limit.

How long should I study for the ASNT Level III exam?

Most successful candidates prepare for 3–6 months following a phased plan, budgeting 8–12 hours of study per week.

Do I need to retake the Basic exam for each method?

No. The Basic exam is passed once. Additional methods only require the corresponding Method (Specific) exam.

How much does the ASNT Level III exam cost?

Exam fees are set by ASNT and change periodically — check ASNT's current fee schedule. Total preparation investment varies by region and scope; if you want structured instructor-led prep, contact Atlantis NDT for a tailored quote within 24 hours.
